insights.title: The bottleneck moved from Amy to Zach's curation
insights.text: Before this call the mental model was 'Amy sources, Amy pushes.' After it: Zach self-searches, hearts, and answers the required questions; Amy submits within a 2-at-a-time platform cap. That means the rate-limiter is now Zach's own stack-ranking discipline (2 highest-fit at a time), not Amy's inbox. Actionable and in Zach's court.

insights.title: Marketplace, not a relationship desk
insights.text: Amy is a genuine, warm advocate but the channel is Paraform's algorithmic match + hiring-manager pipelines she does not own. Do not price the warmth as fit leverage. The submissions win or lose on hard-skill/pedigree screens, per Amy's own read and the Blacksmith outcome.

insights.title: Catch-all resume vs the Schriner leadership-scope lesson
insights.text: Amy wants a maximal keyword catch-all resume to survive ATS/AI matching. That directly tensions with [[technical-cut-resume-must-keep-leadership-scope]]: a keyword-stuffed cut can dilute the builder/team-lead/exec-partner narrative into an IC-only read. The fix is an EXPANSIVE resume that ADDS keyword surface WITHOUT dropping leadership scope - breadth, not compression, and not a de-levelled IC pitch.

next_steps.text: Build the expanded 'catch-all' ATS resume: maximal applied-AI/FDE/product keyword surface AND intact 3-chapter leadership scope (builder → founder 2012-2016 DTC → 2016-present regulated-industry product/transformation: WTA relaunch, rare-disease nonprofit, ARCS). Do NOT let it de-level to IC-only (Schriner lesson). Send to Amy to replace the refined version.

Self-search Paraform, stack-rank to the 2 highest-fit reqs THIS WEEK (allotment is 2): target applied-AI product / forward-deployed product / forward-deployed engineering / senior product lead - NOT staff/senior SWE (Blacksmith archetype). Express interest and answer the required questions so Amy can submit.

Set the salary floor in-profile at $225K base (Zach's stated floor; optimizing for company staying-power/growth over max total comp). Confirm to Amy she may enable the profile-discoverability toggle so hiring managers' keyword searches surface Zach directly (CC to Amy).

Give Amy the 'red thread' narrative for the short-stint / solo-engagement question she flagged ('why you left them... land on what the good story is there'): the 3-chapter arc framed as deliberate independent/embedded senior-operator engagements, not instability.

Amy's court: ask Paraform (her standing Wednesday call) why Blacksmith still shows an open application when she has 'did not move forward' feedback; and check whether remote roles can be surfaced (remote is not a filter she can pull - city-only - so she must open each role to see it).
Timing constraint to hold in view: surgery Friday 2026-09-19, ~1-2 months recovery. Position availability as remote-start ramping to hybrid; front-load the resume + 2 submissions before Friday.

blocks.intro: Amy is a genuinely warm advocate operating on a marketplace she does not own. Read the warmth as relationship equity, not as fit leverage.

items.html: Amy : warm, high-rapport, personally invested ('you have great experience, Zach'). Turned 50 this year, two kids engaged - personal rapport is real and worth maintaining.
The channel : Paraform is an algorithmic marketplace. Amy is newer to it, learning the companies; she explicitly does NOT have deep hiring-manager relationships to trade on here.
Throughput mechanics : 2 submissions at a time until hiring-manager feedback returns, then 2 more. Not a high-volume funnel - some reqs have only 1-2 candidates in pipeline against 4 open roles.
Blacksmith : already submitted (staff/senior product engineer), came back 'did not move forward.' The Paraform record still shows it open; Amy will ask why on her Wednesday call.
Geography : reqs cluster SF / NY, some DC/Baltimore/TX/Canada. Remote is not a filter Amy can pull (city-only); she must open each role to check. Zach is NY-workable, SF no.

blocks.intro: The call's job was to establish who-holds-the-ball at each step and stop wasting tailoring effort on pedigree-mismatched reqs.

items.html: What can each side actually see/do in Paraform? · resolved live via screen-share - Zach can self-search + express interest; Amy submits.
Which reqs are real fits vs pedigree-locked? · Amy: hard-skill focused, but 'they're definitely out there' - needs Zach's own eyeball + stack-rank.
Landmine: mistaking Amy's warmth for hiring-manager leverage. The screens are pedigree/hard-skill driven; Blacksmith proves it.
Landmine: the 'catch-all keyword resume' Amy wants can silently de-level Zach to IC-only - must add keyword surface WITHOUT dropping leadership scope.
Landmine: burning a scarce 2-at-a-time slot on a Blacksmith-shaped SWE req instead of an applied-AI/FDE/product-lead fit.

blocks.close: Net: this is a throughput/curation problem Zach now controls, wrapped around an unresolved fit question that only a named, matched, decision-owner-backed req will close.

items.html: Kairos: the self-search discovery was a live process unlock for BOTH parties - Amy didn't know candidates could self-source. Seize it now while the mental model is fresh: send the resume + 2 stack-ranked submissions before Friday's surgery.
Quiet signal: Amy's pivot from 'I build the list and send it' to 'this is a lot more friendly, you drive' is a real ownership handoff. The relationship is now collaborative, not dependent.
Risk (load-bearing): Blacksmith rejection is the one hard data point and it points at pedigree screening. Warmth cannot GREEN this; only a matched req with a met decision-owner can.
Risk: the catch-all resume de-levelling Zach to IC-only (Schriner-class error). Expand keyword surface, keep leadership scope.
Risk: surgery Friday compresses the window; anything not moved by Thursday slips 1-2 months.

blocks.intro: Adversarial pass on the candidacy, not on Amy.

items.html: BAR (ruin): the exposed edge is opportunity-cost + morale - flooding pedigree-locked reqs burns the scarce 2-slot allotment and stacks Blacksmith-shaped rejections right before surgery. Ration to genuine fits.

LAB · Loki: steel-manned skeptic - Amy's 'they're definitely out there' may be encouragement, not evidence; there is not yet ONE named req where a T-shaped applied-AI operator is the target archetype. Treat req-fit as unproven until a matched role is on the table.
COURT: no overclaim - Zach named his own stop-loss on-call (Waterloo-ML pedigree 'that's not me'), keeping the fit gap explicit rather than papered over.

p: The highest-information event available here is a second matched-then-rejected req: it would confirm the pipeline is warmth-without-fit and reprice the whole channel as low-yield, saving weeks of tailoring - useful calibration for every marketplace-recruiter lead, not just Amy's.

Lossless test (no jargon, to Amy): 'I only want to spend a submission on roles that are actually a fit, so I'll pick the two best each week rather than blast the list - and I'll send you a resume built to be found by the keyword search, without hiding that I've led teams, not just built solo.' Holds intact.
